title: Detecting and repairing reliability issues in operating systems and applications using a generative artificial intelligence system (US 12,711,009 B2)
authors: Rajeev Prabhu Acharya; Siamak Ahari; Vinay Rao (assignee Microsoft Technology Licensing, LLC)
venue_or_publisher: USPTO (granted 18 Aug 2026; pre-grant pub. US 2025/0045148 A1; provisional 31 Jul 2023)
central_claim: An LLM receives error context (exception text, call stack, memory dump, incident report or event log) and code lines for a detected issue, outputs a repaired version, and a pull-request API can return a PR plus a software test.
cite_claim: Granted claims cover error-triggered LLM repair whose dependent claims add a pull request accompanied by a software test; the trigger is a detected failure, not a contract violation in a successful result, and no fail-first or CI gate is claimed.
location: Abstract; claims 1, 8, 9, 11, 12, 15 (OCR of USPTO PDF pp. 1, 24-26)
quote: in response to the pull request, the pull request API provides the pull request and software test for testing the indicated software code.
relevance: Closest patent found: covers Repair and part of Ship (PR + test) for error-triggered issues.

title: Testing software code in a production environment (US 9,983,982 B1)
authors: Surjeet Kumar; Aloysius John; Biju Abraham; Soorej Nair; Priya Nanduri (assignee Visa International Service Association)
central_claim: Production request/response payloads are mirrored to a validation computer running a second software version, whose regenerated payloads are compared with production ones to detect errors.
cite_claim: Prior art for validating a new code version against captured production request/response pairs (a replay gate); no detection on live results, no repair, no PR.
quote: To detect potential errors in the second version, the modified request payload is compared with the request payload
relevance: Covers part of Capture and a replay-style validation gate.

title: Recording network information for test generation (US 12,483,491 B2)
authors: Dezhi Bi; Jianglong Cao; Yalin Chen; et al. (assignee Zoom Communications, Inc.)
central_claim: A browser extension captures API request/response messages and a test-case generation service builds test cases from them.
cite_claim: Prior art for generating tests from a captured API exchange; no violation trigger, no fail-first requirement, no repair.
quote: generates and outputs standardized test information based on the first network information to a test case generation service.
relevance: Covers Capture and part of Reproduce.

title: Adaptive frontend performance diagnosis and remediation (US 12,699,546 B1)
authors: Muthu Selvam; et al. (assignee U.S. Bank National Association)
central_claim: A telemetry anomaly (statistical baseline and ML scoring) in frontend performance is mapped to a code root cause; a code patch is generated and applied; a dependent claim adds review and approval before modifying.
cite_claim: Prior art for runtime-anomaly-triggered generated code patches with optional human approval; performance metrics, not data correctness; no test or PR.
quote: A code patch is generated; the code patch being configured to avoid the anomaly.
relevance: Covers Observe (statistical), Repair, partial Ship (approval).

title: Insecure model context protocol server remediation for artificial intelligence agents (US 12,549,574 B1)
authors: Andrew Morgan; Rahul Parwani (assignee Airia LLC)
venue_or_publisher: USPTO (filed 11 Jul 2025; provisional 30 May 2025; granted 10 Feb 2026)
central_claim: An SSE bridge in front of an MCP server stores the server's resource profile, compares it with later versions, and blocks commands according to security rules.
cite_claim: Granted MCP-proxy patent that detects changes in MCP server resource profiles for security remediation; it does not check tool results for correctness or repair code.
quote: A system detects changes in model context protocol (“MCP”) processes, and performs a remedial action.
relevance: Prior art for an MCP proxy that detects server change; Observe only, security not correctness.

title: Proxy-based secure model context protocol server access for artificial intelligence agents (US 12,562,968 B1)
authors: Morgan et al. (assignee Airia LLC)

quote: A gateway securely executes model context protocol (“MCP”) processes for artificial intelligence (“AI”) agents
relevance: MCP proxy prior art only.
